rendered: Cathode: the anode-free full cell uses presodiated iron pyrite. The authors chose pyrite (FeS2) for the cathode[1] as a cheap, abundant material. Preparation: because pyrite natively contains no sodium, the cathode was presodiated the pyrite cathode prior to cell assembly[2]. Sodium is then removed from the pyrite on the first charge and plated in situ on the carbon/Al collector, so the cell is a sodium metal battery that does not contain sodium metal on assembly[3]. Capacity assumed for the energy density: the calculation used a 335 mAh/g[4] capacity for FeS2, together with the Na1.5FeS2 stoichiometry[5], giving the reported ∼400 Wh/kg[6] energy density, based on the mass of the presodiated pyrite and the carbon nucleation layer.
